topic: Electric eel's 860-volt discharge and why it is a knifefish
title: Electric Eel: The 860-Volt Fish That Isn't an Eel
description:
The electric eel is not a true eel but a knifefish, and a record discharge of 860 volts was measured in 2019. Meet its scores.

#electriceel #animals #nature #shorts

scenes.narration: This animal is called an eel, but it is not an eel at all.

visual.prompt: an electric eel swimming through murky Amazon river water, side view, dim light

scenes.narration: The electric eel is a knifefish that lives in the rivers of South America, and it can grow over two meters long.

visual.prompt: a murky tropical river in the Amazon basin, morning mist, wide shot

scenes.narration: Most of its body is made of cells that work like tiny batteries, stacked in a row to build voltage.

visual.prompt: a long dark fish body with faint electric blue light running along it, cinematic close up

scenes.narration: In 2019, scientists measured a discharge of up to 860 volts from one electric eel, the strongest ever recorded from an animal.

visual.prompt: bright blue electric arcs lighting up dark river water around a fish, dramatic

scenes.narration: It can even leap partly out of the water to press its body on a threat and send the shock straight in.

visual.prompt: an electric eel arching out of the water toward a hand held above it, splash, tense moment

scenes.narration: Attack score: nine out of ten. Defense score: seven, because few predators dare touch it.

visual.prompt: electric blue glow around a dark fish in murky water, low angle

scenes.narration: Would you ever swim near one? Comment your answer and follow for more wild showdowns.
